title: Trial (fixed): The follow-up after the step time; a "did it" with no proof gets a warm ask
origin: #230 trial of fixed lines, from followup-no-proof. Removed once the method is picked.

history.text: Yo Jordan! 30 minutes around the park at 6 tonight, nice and easy. You in?

plan.step: 30 min easy run around the park
plan.reason: Four easy runs a week builds the base.

today_step.step: 30 min easy run around the park

testerLines.say: did it! legs are dead lol
testerLines.when: after ZOH's text asking how the run went

testerLines.say: I forgot to record it on Strava
testerLines.when: after ZOH asks for proof of the run (a Strava screenshot or similar)

whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: no case covered the follow-up nudge and what comes after it.
shouldHaveHappened: A short check-in shortly before 6 is fine. With no word after the step's time and length, one follow-up text ZOH starts itself, asking how it went (1 to 3 sentences, no lecture). "did it!" gets real energy and a quick ask for the run's proof, with no check mark yet. When he forgot to record it, ZOH stays warm and asks for anything he can still send today (a photo or another screenshot, a voice note), says in a few words why proof matters, never accuses him and never caves into counting it without proof.
facts: you ran 30 minutes around the park at 6, easy pace
your legs are tired but it felt good
you forgot to start Strava, so there's no record of the run on your phone
